item.text: {"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"During López Obrador’s 2023 period, Mexico had documented civilian nuclear-safety command, inspection, training, emergency, custody, and corrective-action systems at Laguna Verde. CFE and CNSNS maintained root-cause analysis, safety-culture monitoring, operator training, emergency exercises, spent-fuel storage, post-Fukushima mitigation, and regulatory inspection and sanction powers; the government reported federal funding for operation, training, waste, and decommissioning, but this does not establish adequacy or a presidential resource choice (BATCH-0002-E004; BATCH-0002-E005; BATCH-0002-E007; BATCH-0002-E008; BATCH-0002-E010; BATCH-0002-E011; BATCH-0002-E012; BATCH-0002-E013). The record also shows unresolved weaknesses: CNSNS was technically autonomous but not fully legally or administratively independent, financial and knowledge-management constraints persisted, some sanction proceedings remained pending, no human-and-organizational-factor inspections occurred during 2019–2021, and certain post-Fukushima measures lacked verified full completion by the end of 2023 (BATCH-0002-E002; BATCH-0002-E005; BATCH-0002-E006; BATCH-0002-E009; BATCH-0002-E011). The 2023 radiological-source incidents provide direct contrary evidence: the March theft was rated INES 1 and the sources were recovered without reported harm, after which inspectors verified improved security; the October theft was provisionally rated INES 2 and recorded degradation of defence in depth, although no release, overexposure, injury, or continuing problem was reported (BATCH-0040-E011; BATCH-0038-E002). Broader military-cybersecurity failures are relevant only as qualified evidence of wider catastrophic-risk governance, not as direct proof of nuclear weapons command, custody, or launch controls (BATCH-0011-E005; BATCH-0047-E010; BATCH-0008-E006). The material safeguards and responses are primarily attributable to CFE, CNSNS, SENER, and other agencies; the supplied record does not establish López Obrador’s personal direction, funding decision, or correction of identified nuclear-safety failures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0031-E002","BATCH-0040-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E006","BATCH-0002-E009","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0008-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most detailed nuclear-safety evidence covers 2019–2021 or 2022 and does not directly verify end-2023 implementation.","Government-reported funding, staffing, completion, and safety performance are not independently verified in the supplied record.","BATCH-0002-E008 supports federal/CFE funding and 1,400 permanent CFE Nuclear Corporate Coordination employees as of March 2022, not adequate staffing or a personal presidential choice.","Evidence concerns civilian nuclear and radiological safety more than nuclear weapons custody, launch authority, or strategic command-and-control.","The supplied record does not establish López Obrador’s personal direction, knowledge, or corrective action."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported unqualified claim that safeguards were simply “funded and staffed”; funding and staffing are now attributed and qualified.","Corrected the temporal framing by distinguishing direct 2023 incidents from earlier institutional evidence and unverified planned completion by end-2023.","Reclassified military cybersecurity evidence as broader, qualified catastrophic-risk governance rather than direct nuclear command-and-control evidence.","Distinguished the March 2023 INES 1 theft, including recovery and verified improved security, from the October 2023 provisional INES 2 theft and its documented defence-in-depth degradation.","Preserved the mixed institutional record, contrary evidence, attribution limits, and uncertainty about effectiveness and corrective-action closure."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Direct end-2023 evidence is needed on nuclear-safety implementation, corrective-action closure, inspection activity, staffing, funding adequacy, waste-storage capacity, and post-Fukushima measures.","The ledger should seek evidence specifically addressing Mexican nuclear-weapons custody or strategic command authority, if any, rather than relying on civilian nuclear safety as a proxy.","The March and October 2023 radiological-source incidents warrant any available investigation or follow-up records concerning preventive controls and durable remediation."]}
